statement: You are given a grid of letters board and a string word. In board the rows are written left to right and separated by commas, so "ABCE,SFCS" is a grid with two rows of four letters.
The word is found if it can be spelled by a path of cells where each cell is next to the previous one horizontally or vertically. A cell may be used at most once in the path.
Return true if word can be found in board, and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Start at the top-left A, go right through B and C, down to the C below it, down to E and left to D.
A, B, C can be spelled along the top row, but the only B next to that C is the one already used, and a cell may not be reused.

constraints: 1 ≤ number of rows, number of columns ≤ 6
board and word consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters
